families.name: Primary booking actions
families.difference: The route/timing action applies a 1.3 desktop scale to Button; the vehicle action uses an unscaled full-width Button with its own text size. Compare rendered height, text, radius and padding below.
families.rationale: These are successive primary actions in the same legacy booking flow. The commit step may deliberately differ from the earlier steps; no approved reference establishes one standard.
families.cascade: Button is reused outside these screens. Any future choice must be scoped to the listed booking actions; global Button or brand-token edits are excluded.

families.name: Address text fields
families.difference: Booking uses the shared Input with desktop vertical scaling, medium text and marker/clear adornments. Saved places uses a local unscaled input inside an account row. Measure the shared address-entry task while preserving the distinct page themes.
families.rationale: Both accept a place address, but booking offers autocomplete and Settings edits a saved address. Theme and available width are deliberate context differences; the intended common control proportions need an owner choice.
families.cascade: Only pickup, drop and the saved Home editor are sampled. Settings reuses its editor for Work and custom places: those variants remain unverified and need an expanded affected-controls review before any edit that would reach them. Other Input callers are excluded. Colors and autocomplete behavior are locked.

families.name: Selection controls: compact modes and rich cards
families.difference: Trip mode uses compact pill buttons. Vehicle choice uses larger cards with a vehicle image, passenger count and sample fare. Both expose aria-pressed; their content and space requirements differ.
families.rationale: Different information density justifies distinct shapes. This is an explicit exception candidate, not a confirmed visual defect. Do not turn vehicle cards into pills or trip-mode choices into fare cards.
families.cascade: Preserve the P06 selected-state fix and the existing trip-mode behavior. A pattern decision here never approves a booking-rule change.
